doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

title: Nick's in Greenwich Village: hours and pay
summary: Igoe played steady Dixieland at Nick's from 1954 for $150-180 a week, far above Village Vanguard pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh I think so, especially in the days when I got to stay home. See I spent an awful lot of time on the road. And so I started to stay home. I had a good Dixieland career down in Nick’s in Greenwich Village when it was the place for Dixieland. And actually that was the best steady jazz job in New York at the time. And so I played there for three or four years. And that was after I had finished with Charlie Ventura’s group. And I played there for about three or four years. So finally, it’s not like okay you have a job for six months and then you’re off for three or something like that. This was like a year round thing, six nights a week and a Sunday afternoon.

Oh yeah. We worked from — the hours were 9:30 to 4 on weeknights, 9 to 3 on Saturday night and Sunday afternoon from 5 to 9 and then 10 to 3. That was the week. And it was marvelous. All great musicians, and it really was a fun job.
Can I ask how much you were making for those kind of hours?

Yes we were making — I started at $150 a week. Three days later after I had started I got a telegram from the leader saying, “I’m giving you a $30 raise.” So I went to $180. But that was unheard of in a jazz club in New York. The guys up the street — I won’t mention names — but the guys up the street at the Village Vanguard were putting in — they didn’t have a Sunday afternoon matinee but they had six nights like we did, the same hours until 4 in the morning that — New York was going until 4 in the morning in those days because you could walk the streets, there was no problems. And I’d meet some of these guys. There was a diner midway between us so we’d all have a cup of coffee and meet some of these guys, some guys you know. “Hey what are you doing?” “Well I’m up at the Vanguard, man. What are you doing?” “I’m playing at Nick’s.” “Oh, hey what are you making down there?” I said, “I’m making $180.” He says, “what? $180?” I says, “well what are you guys making up there?” He says, “$80.” 80 bucks a week.
